newsitem.title: UK: Dirty oil tanker rates firmer but trade slow.
newsitem.headline: Dirty oil tanker rates firmer but trade slow.

text.p: Oil tanker chartering activity got off to a slow start on Monday with prospective charterers deterred by expensive late October freight costs, brokers said.
"There's a fair ammount of demand for tonnage pegged around third decade October, but tight avails, particularly of Aframax (80,000 tonne) vessels has pushed rates up a bit," one said.
Aframax tonnage for late October inter-UK/Cont voyage was reported booked up to around W117.5 today, up sharply compared with last week's levels of around W100 for similar fixings.
UKC Suezmax rates were also stronger towards the end of the month with W97.5 paid for an end-Oct lifting, up 12 points.
Caribbean upcoast U.S. voyages were also firmer for 70,000 tonne cargoes with deliveries into the U.S. Gulf valued around 2-1/2 points higher at W135.

In the Mideast Gulf/Red Seas loading sector ULCCS were seen trading to the West at W47.5 and a VLCC with USG/UKC options was fixed at a steady W52.5/W55 respectively. Rates for Japan pegged around last traded levels of W62.5. A VLCC was booked for Oct 26 loading, but no rate was reported.
No Singapore fixings for VLCCs were reported but levels for this trip valued steady at W52.5, based on a fixing for Thailand delivery at W49.

Tight modern tonnage saw prompt West African/USG shipments holding firm but end-Oct/early-Nov fixings were slightly softer with Suezmax cargoes fixed out of Cabinda and Gamba to the U.S. Gulf at W102.5.
